motions.description: Put Quaternius CC0 clips on a rigged character. params.clips is a list of library clip names (Walk_Loop, or ual2/Melee_Hook when the name is in both packs). Search them with hawkesgen_library (tags: locomotion, melee, hit, death, idle). inputs.files[0] is the character (GLB/FBX, asset:<id> or slot:./rig). params.entity is project/slug: each clip is filed on that character as animation/<name>. params.preview true also renders a video per clip. The library is the free Standard editions, not the paid full packs.

character3d.description: THE recipe for a 3D character from a concept image (inputs.files[0]), always from four views, never one: A-pose front view -> cutout -> image.viewsheet (true back, left and right views of the same character, flat even light on grey, each cut out; Claude checks all four are the same character and a bad view is made again before any 3D GPU time is spent; the sheet is saved as a library asset) -> mesh.views3d (Pixal3D multi-view + TRELLIS.2, PBR GLB; best of 3) -> Blender: report, fix, symmetrize, retopo to ~8k quads, bake from the raw mesh, report, LODs, budget, web GLB, collision -> mesh.rig. Saves: apose, cutout, sheet, raw, mesh (GLB + LODs), rig. For robots and creatures with their limbs spread (Spider Bot, Yo Bot) set form creature on the image.viewsheet step (the kind character3d does it from data.form). Heavy: five models of about 9 GB (workflows/mesh-views3d). The GPU chain is untested end to end. Docs: docs/3d-characters.md.

params.pick: Matches the concept from every angle: correct proportions and silhouette, on-model with the reference, symmetric, no shards, spikes or holes, clean texture on front, back and sides.

params.prompt: same character, A-pose (or a neutral standing pose for a creature), arms about 45 degrees down, legs apart, front view, plain flat light grey background (no checkerboard, no transparency grid, no shadow), flat even lighting. Keep the exact same design, colors and proportions. Full body from head to feet, facing the viewer, nothing else in the picture.

character3d-mv.description: Old name of shared/character3d: a humanoid from four views (the front+back two-view recipe with a single-image mesh was retired).

character3d-4v.description: Same as shared/character3d (the four-view recipe is now the default).

prop3d.description: A textured GLB prop from a reference image (inputs.files[0], the object seen straight from the front on a plain background), always from four views, never one: cutout -> image.viewsheet (form prop: back, left and right views of the same object, checked for consistency) -> mesh.views3d. Convert/compress the GLB before shipping. A prop where one view is truly enough can use mesh.textured with allowSingleView true.
